reference.title: Dumbbell Standing Inner Biceps Curl
reference.listing: Page could not be read (gymvisual.com blocked by the proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s up, short squeeze, about 2.5 s down, brief pause in the stretch

prescription.progression: Load is user-chosen: pick a dumbbell you can curl for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion); add reps, then weight. Use a lighter dumbbell than for the regular incline curl (clinical opinion).

cues.text: Stand tall, feet about hip width. Let the arms hang a little out from the sides, turned out, palms facing forward and out.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbells up and out toward the outside of the shoulders, keeping the elbows where they hang.
Squeeze with the palms facing the shoulders; chest up, no lean back.
Breathe in and lower slowly along the same arc to straight arms.
Pause briefly with straight arms, then repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the elbows drift in to the ribs
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows a hand width out and the arms turned out.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning back to swing the weight
mistakes.fix: Stand tall with a braced trunk; go lighter.
Keep the wrists straight in line with the forearms.

kinematics.norm: Full range: mean elbow range was about 117-123 degrees across barbell, EZ-bar and alternating dumbbell curls (Marcolin 2018)

kinematics.measure: Forearm rotation (wrist pron channel, 0 = palm up/forward, 90 = thumb up)
kinematics.norm: The supinated grip gave the highest biceps activity in the lifting phase; neutral grips shift work toward the brachioradialis (Coratella 2023)

kinematics.measure: Upper arm from the trunk line (sagittal)
kinematics.norm: Elbows stay near the sides; a small forward drift at the top is normal, a big swing shifts work to the front deltoid (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 1 s up and 2-3 s down (clinical opinion); biceps activity was lower while lowering than lifting at the same load (Oliveira 2009)

kinematics.measure: Arm abduction (upper arm out from the trunk)
kinematics.norm: Arms angled out from the sides with the shoulders turned out, so the forearms curl out instead of straight ahead (clinical opinion)
Standing tall, feet about hip width, trunk still (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual Dumbbell Standing Inner Biceps Curl, video page (movement reference; page not readable here)
Oliveira, Matta, Alves, Garcia and Vieira 2009, effect of the shoulder position on the biceps brachii EMG in different dumbbell curls (J Sports Sci Med 8(1):24-29; PMC3737788)
Coratella et al. 2023, biceps brachii and brachioradialis excitation in biceps curl exercise: different handgrips, different synergy (Sports 11(3):64; PMC10054060)
Marcolin et al. 2018, differences in electromyographic activity of biceps brachii and brachioradialis while performing three variants of curl (PeerJ 6:e5165; PMC6047503)

cautions: Elbow or shoulder pain: lighten the dumbbell and shorten the range; stop if pain is sharp (clinical opinion).
Keep the wrists straight (in line with the forearm); a bent-back wrist under load strains the forearm (clinical opinion).
Pick the dumbbells up and set them down with a straight back and bent knees.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Front-of-shoulder pain in the turned-out position: bring the elbows in closer to the sides (clinical opinion).
modify: Shoulder discomfort: regular standing curl with the arms by the sides.
progressions: Slower lowering with a pause in the stretch.

muscleNotes.biceps_r: Main elbow flexor; on the incline the shoulder starts extended (long head stretched). Turning the arms out with the palms facing forward and out is commonly said to bias the short (inner) head; we found no study measuring this (clinical opinion). Incline curls trained the proximal elbow flexors more than preacher curls (Kassiano 2025).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Main elbow flexor; on the incline the shoulder starts extended (long head stretched). Turning the arms out with the palms facing forward and out is commonly said to bias the short (inner) head; we found no study measuring this (clinical opinion). Incline curls trained the proximal elbow flexors more than preacher curls (Kassiano 2025).
muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_r: Brachioradialis (mapped to the forearm extensor region) assists elbow flexion, most with the forearm near neutral.
muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_l: Brachioradialis (mapped to the forearm extensor region) assists elbow flexion, most with the forearm near neutral.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Wrist and finger flexors hold the handle and keep the wrist straight.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Wrist and finger flexors hold the handle and keep the wrist straight.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Steadies the shoulder in the stretched, turned-out position.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Steadies the shoulder in the stretched, turned-out position.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk upright so the curl does not turn into a swing.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Holds the arms turned out (external rotation) through the set.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Holds the arms turned out (external rotation) through the set.

Elbow bends through a full range
